cards.proof_strategy: Use the derivative hypothesis to obtain the punctured difference-quotient limit u.
sketch_steps: Use the derivative hypothesis to obtain the punctured difference-quotient limit u.
Interpret the quotient only off zero when taking this limit.
Replace its value at zero by u.
The continuous-update criterion now proves continuity of the constructed extension.

cards.canonical_statement: For every real a, the product |x-a|·|x-a| has derivative zero at a, although each factor |x-a| is not differentiable at a.
cards.proof_strategy: Rewrite the product of absolute values as (x-a)².
sketch_steps: Rewrite the product of absolute values as (x-a)².
Differentiate this polynomial to obtain derivative zero at a.
Translate the supposed derivative of |x-a| at a back to that of |x| at zero.
The known cusp contradiction shows that differentiability of a product need not imply differentiability of its factors.

cards.canonical_statement: If c>0, f′=h everywhere, h(a)=0, and h(y)-h(x)≥2c(y-x) whenever x≤y, then f(x)≥f(a)+c(x-a)² for every x. A uniformly increasing derivative yields a quantitative global minimum bound.
cards.proof_strategy: Subtract the quadratic c(x-a)² from f and call the result g.
sketch_steps: Subtract the quadratic c(x-a)² from f and call the result g.
Its derivative is h(x)-2c(x-a).
The assumed slope-growth inequality makes this new derivative nondecreasing.
Hence g is globally convex, and h(a)=0 makes g stationary at a.
Compare both left and right secant slopes against the zero derivative to get g(a)≤g(x).
Expand g and rearrange to obtain the global quadratic growth bound for f.
